scope: Retained Netlink raw/vector/message/batch I/O, supported route/link/address changes, non-publishing netfilter/conntrack calls, and actual queue-driven receive/poll/epoll wakeups on execution workers; preserve joined nf_tables ruleset publication.
method: Four independent processes each perform 1,000 checked request/reply iterations; four Trames vCPUs; three unprofiled counterbalanced samples plus one separate diagnostic repeat. RTM_GETLINK requests query interface index 1 without dump; each reply is checked for declared length, RTM_NEWLINK type, sequence and interface index. Vector/message variants use two iovecs. Poll checks actual readiness before receive. Endpoint setup/cleanup is outside the loop timer. Native ARM Linux runs the identical static musl ELF on six vCPUs. All release builds, initial affected CI and FFI checks finish before timing; local Linux is stopped during Mac timing. A final test-only epoll assertion is validated afterward without changing the measured production code. TCP/pipe controls also run through native macOS APIs. No native macOS Netlink substitute is used.

comparison_limits.note: The identical query returns different attribute sets and response byte counts in the two kernels; native Linux is a contextual reference, not byte-for-byte identical reply processing. macOS has no native Netlink API. Controls show no observed degradation; no control gain or statistical regression bound is claimed. Results do not establish whole-app, Firefox, physical-iPad or universally native performance.

cases: Scalar/vector/sendto/sendmsg/kernel-sendmmsg route query results retain source, sequence and interface identity
Pending receive survives FD close/reuse and wakes from the real resource without a reactor
Actual epoll_ctl and epoll_wait retain original weak OFD identity and event data after numeric reuse
Poll snapshots and watches do not pin final socket close
Notification callback receives and changes options on the same socket after original gates release
Namespace FD resolution precedes topology writer; canonical error ACK and error order are preserved
Top-level and nested veth-peer namespace targets retain actual shared namespace OFDs and identity through notification flush
Missing namespace FD returns EBADF; wrong type returns EINVAL; missing NET_ADMIN preserves prior EPERM
Final target namespace teardown occurs outside topology and source socket gates
sendmmsg keeps completed query progress and accepted source across nf_tables owner handoff and FD reuse, without replay
Distinct guest processes with one/two execution slots exchange link multicast, poll, response ACK and recvmsg on workers
validation.reuse: The final epoll assertion is cfg(test)-only: its affected Apple/Linux ABI case and strict checks rerun; full ABI/VFS/net/kernel passes and unchanged production artifacts are reused. The strengthened distinct-process kernel case is included in final full278 passes. The final common contract paragraph is documentation-only. CPU/memory/graphics acceptance and unchanged guest artifacts are reused. No production source changes after builds or performance samples.
validation.resolved_fixture_failure: An initial new VFS test attempted unsupported bridge namespace placement. It was corrected to the already-supported veth with top-level and peer targets; final full VFS passes, without a production compatibility workaround.

implementation.ownership: Actual shared SocketOperation and complete namespace OFDs retain the creating socket namespace, accepted credentials, copied current input/output and batch progress. Numeric FD reuse cannot substitute an accepted source or namespace target.
implementation.readiness: Actual Netlink queues own shared readiness. Reply and multicast sources are deduplicated and notified after queue, registry, topology and outer Socket gates release. Existing subscriptions release execution slots; poll resources stay weak. No reactor is needed for internal Netlink waits.
implementation.namespace_lock_order: Resolve schema-defined namespace FD attributes before topology writer, once per target number per request. Canonical validators still select errors at original points. Retain target Network refs beyond graph release and actual namespace OFDs beyond outer Socket release and notification flush.
implementation.policy_publication: Only NETLINK_NETFILTER messages beginning with NFNL_MSG_BATCH_BEGIN defer through the original accepted-entry owner boundary. Publishing a new ruleset could invalidate captured policy-free native TCP capabilities; retain this invariant rather than adding a per-byte permission/generation check or memory barrier.
implementation.existing_paths: Existing accepted native TCP and shared pipe/device/Unix byte capabilities return before the new socket fallback. Already-connected native TCP keeps its selected transport across route/link updates. No extra ordinary guest-memory check or native-only permission policy.
implementation.synchronization: Existing object-local resource locks and notification sources; no new global resource lock, coordinator/service thread, polling bus, ordinary guest fence or unsafe code.

remaining: nf_tables ruleset publication and invalidation of captured native TCP policy-free capabilities
Unix-bearing owning ancillary graphs and cycle reclamation
Task/job control, pending task signals and mount/proc ownership
Structural file/VM/task transitions and residual whole-process cohort joins
recvmmsg is unimplemented, not a migrated coordinator dependency
